t: You're on Curzon Street in Mayfair, which runs from Fitzmaurice Place, past Shepherd Market, to Park Lane. It is named after Sir Nathaniel Curzon, who inherited the land in 1715, and more houses went up here in the 1720s. The prime minister Benjamin Disraeli died on this street. So did Admiral Sir George Pocock, who served in the Seven Years' War. Georgiana Curzon, a socialite, was born here, and the chocolate manufacturer Laurence Cadbury lived here. The street also gives its name to George Howe, Viscount Howe, whom James Wolfe called the best officer in the British Army.
